reporting_rule: Missing information is recorded as not reported. Reviewer-inferred risks are explicitly labeled and are not observations.

relationship_definition.core: The system performs qualitative coding or theme work, or directly evaluates an LLM qualitative-analysis workflow.
relationship_definition.adjacent: The paper isolates a validity, leakage, contamination, privacy, or evaluation mechanism that materially affects core-system design or evaluation.

papers.citation: Yu D, Liu Z, He H. Same Company, Same Signal: The Role of Identity in Earnings Call Transcripts. Findings of ACL 2025:18403-18422.
papers.objective: Test whether transcript representations and predictions encode repeated company identity rather than task-relevant semantics.
papers.runs_seeds_hardware: Single model-evaluation run; trained systems seed 2021; dataset random state 42; NVIDIA L40.
principal_results: Direct GPT-4o and Gemini prediction MSE .345 and .339; embedding methods average .260-.269; Random(Ticker) .265; STPEV(mean) .252; Random(All) .323; PEV(mean) .307.
Within-ticker/full-dataset mean cosine: OpenAI vanilla .900/.700; Gecko .958/.865; GPT-4o summary .920/.685; GPT-4o task .929/.724; Gemini summary .931/.713; Gemini task .918/.728; average .937/.738.
Transcript predictions correlated with STPEV(mean) at average r=.847 over 2021-2023; yearly means .815/.852/.874; Random(All) .183/.007/.004.
papers.ethics_privacy: not reported as a material issue for public corporate transcripts
limitations: Similarity and correlation evidence, not a causal counterfactual decomposition.
papers.review_implication: Clinical qualitative systems should test participant/site/interviewer/diagnosis/source-disjoint evaluation, source probes, boilerplate and metadata masking, and counterfactual source swaps.

papers.citation: Ashwin J, Chhabra A, Rao V. Using Large Language Models for Qualitative Analysis can Introduce Serious Bias. Sociological Methods & Research. Online 2025; issue 55(3):795-839, 2026.
papers.methodology_claimed: deductive qualitative coding with LLMs versus supervised iQual
papers.domain: Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts, Cox's Bazar

dataset.languages: Bengali or Rohingya; transcribed Bengali; machine-translated and corrected English

papers.evaluation: Each iQual model fitted 25 times with a randomized 200-interview test set; F1; error regressions on respondent attributes; joint F-tests; downstream regression distortion.
principal_results: Mean F1: iQual .542; iQual plus augmentation .541; GPT-3.5 .414; GPT-4o-mini .390; Llama-3-8B .371; Llama-2-13B .290.
All LLMs overpredicted sparse codes.
GPT-3.5 errors significantly related to respondent characteristics in 10/19 codes at the 5% level; iQual in 1/19.
Interviewer-identity bias test was negative in the authors' Figure A.4.
Generated labels can distort downstream regression estimates.
papers.ethics_privacy: Confidential transcripts; anonymized data available upon request; interviewer ethics training described; IRB and consent details not reported in the verified publisher full text.
papers.reproducibility: Public code; anonymized data on request.
papers.efficiency: Study-time estimates: expert coding about US$10,000; GPT-3.5 about US$600; GPT-4o-mini about US$150; GPT-4 about US$20,000.
papers.review_implication: Aggregate agreement must be supplemented with participant-attribute error models and downstream estimand tests. Generic deductive-bias novelty is partly occupied.

papers.citation: Xu et al. TAMA: A Human-AI Collaborative Thematic Analysis Framework Using Multi-Agent LLMs for Clinical Interviews. ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare. 2026.
papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
papers.architecture: Sequential generation, evaluation, and refinement roles with expert stopping; structured multi-role prompting rather than demonstrated autonomous agent organization.
papers.parameters: GPT-4o temperature 0; other parameters not reported.
papers.human_reference: Three coders: cardiac surgeon plus two qualitative researchers; all transcripts and consensus; about 30 hours per coder.
papers.metrics_statistics: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 threshold .60; Jaccard; hit rate; MICS; 10,000 bootstrap samples; permutation tests.
principal_results: Human: Jaccard .33 (95% CI .25-.71), hit 1.00, MICS .53.
Jaccard decrease versus single GPT-4o p=.022, Cohen h=.27; hit increase p=.250.
Llama-3.1-8B: single Jaccard .20/hit .12; TAMA .68/.08; its evaluator accepted poor themes first pass at 4.40/5.
One-transcript grounding audit reported 13 themes and zero hallucinations.
papers.ethics_privacy: Deidentified data; IRB, consent, proprietary-API retention/training, security configuration, and BAA not reported.
papers.reproducibility: Code public; raw clinical transcripts not public.
validity_concerns: Expert who defined criteria/stopped refinement helped create the original reference themes.
Five lay reviewers independent but qualitative expertise not reported.
Grounding audit used one structured transcript and no external false-negative measure.
Theme hit rate is not participant-level coverage.
Reviewer-inferred contamination risk because public themes/domain labels could have appeared in pretraining; no contamination test; memorization not demonstrated.

papers.citation: Raza et al. LLM-TA: An LLM-Enhanced Thematic Analysis Pipeline for Transcripts from Parents of Children with Congenital Heart Disease. arXiv:2502.01620. 2025.
papers.dataset: Same 9 focus groups/42 parents/12 published themes as TAMA; median 11,457 words/transcript; chunks at most 1,500 words.
papers.evaluation: sentence-T5-XXL threshold .82; all-mpnet .62; all-MiniLM .56; LLM-judge threshold .5; one original expert evaluates.
principal_results: Sentence-T5 Mathis baseline no Reflexion .111/.667 Jaccard/hit; with Reflexion .139/.583.
LLM-TA zero .410/1.00; one .396/1.00; one plus Reflexion .222/1.00.
LLM-judge values zero .118/.750; one .174/.917; one plus Reflexion .152/.917.
Rare dramatic events, including cardiac arrests and financial concerns, were overrepresented; broad themes were sometimes misinterpreted.
papers.efficiency: Most variants under 10 minutes; one-shot plus Reflexion about 90 minutes; human analysis about 30 person-hours per coder.
papers.ethics_privacy: Deidentification reported; IRB, consent, API retention/training, and vendor-security settings not reported.
papers.validity_concerns: Same evaluator nonindependence and reviewer-inferred public-reference contamination risk as TAMA; no participant-level evidence matrix or controlled negative-case test.

papers.citation: Mathis et al. Inductive thematic analysis of healthcare qualitative interviews using open-source large language models: How does it compare to traditional methods? Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine. 2024;255:108356.
papers.dataset: 21 semi-structured interviews: 14 clients with severe mental illness and 7 clinicians; client median 10.5 minutes/1,560 words; clinician median 19.2 minutes/3,244 words.
papers.transcription: Whisper; interviewer and interviewee merged without speaker diarization.
papers.human_reference: 96 client and 180 clinician codes, collapsed to 31/43 unique codes; 6/7 themes.
papers.hardware: Ubuntu; dual RTX 3090; 48 GB total VRAM
papers.metrics_results: Three evaluations; Jaccard .44-.69, described as moderate to substantial.
papers.runs_prompts_seeds: Exact run design beyond the three evaluations, exact prompts/order sensitivity, and seeds not reported.
papers.ethics_privacy: Yale IRB exempt; local PHI/HIPAA-oriented processing; consent not reported.
papers.validity_concern: Merged speaker turns create an untested interviewer/source shortcut.

papers.relationship: core methods/ethics; excluded from clinical-interview subset
papers.citation: Prescott et al. Comparing the Efficacy and Efficiency of Human and Generative AI: Qualitative Thematic Analyses. JMIR AI. 2024;3:e54482.
papers.dataset: 40 investigator-authored intervention SMS prompts, 5-14 words and under 160 characters; not participant-generated.
principal_results: Inductive theme overlap 5/7 (71%) for both models.
Deductive overlap ChatGPT 6/12 (50%), Bard 7/12 (58%).
Coding agreement ChatGPT inductive 31/66 (47%), deductive 22/59 (37%); Bard 20/54 (37%), 21/58 (36%).
Mean time GenAI 20 minutes (SD 3.5) versus human 567 (SD 106.5).
papers.ethics_privacy: Authors did not upload participant-generated SMS because consent did not authorize third-party vendor processing and tools could retain inputs for training; proxy data used; IRB exempt.
papers.review_implication: Deidentification is not authorization; assess consent, data-use scope, processor role, retention, and training terms separately.

papers.citation: Li et al. Comparing GPT-4 and Human Researchers in Health Care Data Analysis: Qualitative Description Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2024;26:e56500.
papers.dataset: 20 adults with acquired buried penis; 15-30 minute interviews; 85% White; 95% heterosexual; mean age 58.8; mean BMI 41.1.
principal_results: 63 code-presence agreements, 14 code-absence agreements, 23 disagreements; kappa .401.
One transcript repeated 10 times: body image and chronic pain 10/10; depression 9/10; less common codes 6-8/10 or fewer.
Human analysis produced richer subthemes.
papers.ethics_privacy: UCSF IRB 20-32062 and consent; secondary GPT-4 analysis exempt; private Versa instance did not retain/train during method development; commercial GPT-4 used after deidentification; commercial retention/settings not reported.
papers.limitations: Single site, narrow demographics, no order tests, no participant-level rare-case metric.

papers.citation: Bijker et al. ChatGPT for Automated Qualitative Research: Content Analysis. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2024;26:e59050.
papers.dataset: Open forum posts; abstract reports 537 and methods report 539; 108-post 20% subset for human verification.
papers.run_design: Four accounts/computers; 10 coding schemes times 10 conversations; structured matrix; 10 unconstrained inductive schemes.
papers.principal_results: Mechanism precision 66%-88%; kappa .72-.82 inductive, .58-.73 deductive/structured; category kappa .67-.95 inductive and .13-.87 deductive.
papers.ethics_privacy: Open posts without identifiers; ethics exempt; prompts/supplement public.
papers.review_implication: Reliability/stability is not evidential validity or fairness.

papers.citation: Bennis and Mouwafaq. Advancing AI-driven thematic analysis: a comparative study of nine generative models on Cutaneous Leishmaniasis data. BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making. 2025;25:124.
papers.dataset: 448 anonymized student quotations from 454 approached and 6 refusals; one short open question; 79 affected (35 female/44 male), 63 nonempty.
papers.run_design: Each coding scheme twice; theme generation four iterations.
principal_results: External weighted kappa: o1-Pro .79 (.74-.85); Claude .78 (.73-.84); Llama .78 (.72-.83).
Human initial kappa .74, targeted second coding .82.
o1-Pro internal kappa 1.00 for affected subgroup.
Four models reached all 24 subthemes/Jaccard 1.00 after combining iterations.
papers.fairness_analysis: Gender chi-square/Fisher tests; residual error bias tests not reported.
papers.ethics_privacy: Original ethics approval; secondary anonymized analysis required no new approval; authors report ephemeral storage and deletion after download; supplements public.
papers.validity_concerns: Published human reference, Perplexity-generated reference synthesis, NotebookLM comparison, and unioned iterations create circularity/reviewer-inferred contamination risk; no direct contamination test.

papers.citation: Hill et al. Large language models for thematic analysis in healthcare research: A blinded mixed-methods comparison with human analysts. PLOS Digital Health. 2026;5(4):e0001189.
papers.dataset: One approximately 2-hour focus group; 7 adults with long-term conditions; 12,172 words.
papers.human_reference: Deductive 10-code/6-theme codebook; expert inductive 14-code/5-theme reference; humans and models mutually blinded; quote plus segment ID required; facilitator segments excluded.
principal_results: Deductive agreement LLM 93.5% (95% CI 92.5-94.5), kappa .34 (.26-.40); human 92.7% (91.6-93.9), kappa .34.
Gwet AC1 LLM .93 (.92-.94), human .92 (.90-.93); code prevalence 7.8% (SD 3.2).
Only ChatGPT-5 inductive noninferiority p=.043.
Strict hallucination 1.2% (SD 2.1); expanded 8.6% (SD 5.1); comprehensive error 12.4%, much driven by facilitator speech.
papers.ethics_privacy: Southampton ERGO 106517; written consent and separate secondary-use opt-out; anonymized; secure institutional environments; transcript withheld for residual identifiability; code/prompts public.
papers.limitations: One transcript; common AI-in-health discourse may be overrepresented in training and inflate alignment; participant-level negative-case metric not reported.

papers.citation: Vikan et al. Reflecting on LLM Support in Reflexive Thematic Analysis: An Exploratory Study. Qualitative Health Research. Online 2025;36(2-3):191-205, 2026 issue.
papers.dataset: One Norwegian operating-room nurse interview; 10 pages/9,262 words; from a 223-page/158,865-word corpus; moderator removed.
papers.model: Offline Mistral-7B through Ollama/HuggingFace with RAG
papers.hardware: RTX 4070 Ti Super, AMD Ryzen 7, 32 GB
papers.run_design: Seven tests, 2024-11-11 through 2025-01-06; 50,009 words of prompts/responses/memos.
papers.principal_results: Poor Norwegian output; English translation improved output but risked semantic loss; omitted essential content; fabricated quotes and page/line references; changed theme meanings; retrieval theory documents contaminated analysis; no time saving.
papers.ethics_privacy: Regional Committee reference 461904; Sikt 307019; written digital information explicitly covered LLM use/privacy/voluntariness; encrypted consent; offline sensitive server.
papers.accountability: Humans, not the LLM, remain authors and accountable for interpretations and outputs.

papers.citation: Grover et al. Advancing the science of qualitative patient preference assessment using large language models. PLOS Digital Health. 2026;5(3):e0001263.
papers.dataset: Five pan-Canadian focus groups; 28 people with cancer history; one French group translated; median 10,097 words, mean 9,491, nearly 50,000 total; human themes member-checked.
papers.hardware_parameters: Windows, RTX 4070, 64 GB; context 34,500; temperature 1, top-p .15, min-p .02, repetition 1.15, top-k 40.
principal_results: Median cosine .80/.79/.81; median Jaccard .60/.46/.64; hit rate .86 for all.
Jaccard p=.41 and hit p=.93; at threshold .82 Jaccard .34/.23/.46.
RAG versus ITS cosine false-discovery-adjusted p=.03.
Naive RAG hallucinated an unrelated compensation-and-incentives debate.
ITS analyst execution about 3.5 hours.
papers.ethics_privacy: REB H20-00861; consent explicitly allowed deidentified secondary research; data access requires REB; local processing.
papers.limitations: One dataset/model/embedding; independent human evaluation of new themes not reported; reviewer-inferred public-reference contamination risk not tested.

papers.citation: Bai and Finkelstein. JMIR Medical Informatics. 2026;14:e96129.
papers.dataset: 48 deidentified interviews: ILD 17 transcripts/169 codes/7 themes; POTS 15/178/10; COPD 16/261/6; not publicly released before analysis.
papers.workflow: Code extraction, code combination, theme generation; L1/L2/L3, direct coding, direct grouping; parent-ID provenance and programmatic ID validation.
papers.evaluation: sentence-T5-XXL, Hungarian assignment, greedy full matching; one run per model/workflow condition.
principal_results: Opus examples: POTS direct .893 (SD .041); COPD direct grouping .891 (.027); ILD L3 .889 (.032).
Opus output 15-60 extraction codes and 43-153 merged codes; Gemini roughly 10 and ChatGPT roughly 25, suggesting model-specific output ceilings.
papers.human_evaluation: One researcher handled output/formats; interrater reliability not reported.
papers.ethics_privacy: Secondary deidentified analysis not human-subjects research; original University of Utah IRB 00168937 and consent; consumer-interface retention/training/enterprise protections not reported.
papers.validity_concerns: Each condition once; no stability test; disease background provided, so domain cues remain.

papers.citation: Turner et al. Large language models for deductive qualitative content analysis in dementia-focused embedded pragmatic clinical trials: A comparative methodological study. Implementation Science Communications. 2026;7:130.
papers.dataset: 10 deidentified six-month interviews; at most 2 participants/transcript; 3,376-9,262 words; four human coders double-coded an 11-code descriptive/interpretive codebook.
papers.deployment_parameters: OpenAI API; temperature 1; top-p 1; 128k context; maximum 5,000 tokens; V4 two runs/model.
principal_results: V3 captured 327/530 human excerpts (61.7%), transcript range 42.4%-72.6%.
Descriptive 214/336 (63.7%); interpretive 112/194 (57.7%).
206 correct excerpts missed by humans; 396/929 (42.6%) extracted excerpts incorrect.
V4 site-characteristic match at 85% combined-run threshold: GPT-4o 48/54 (89%); mini 37/54 (69%).
Word-count correlations r=.230 and -.452.
Estimated 97% time and 99% cost reduction; about US$1 versus .04 per transcript, compared with estimated US$100/5 hours human.
papers.ethics_privacy: Brown IRB 2011002838; restricted raw transcripts; codebook/scripts/examples shared; anonymized and no health information; API retention, BAA, vendor security, and consent for processing not reported.
papers.validity_concerns: Exact-quote matching prevents fabricated strings but not wrong coding; arbitrary Levenshtein thresholds; efficiency excludes full verification burden.

papers.citation: Sakaguchi, Sakama, Watari. Evaluating ChatGPT in Qualitative Thematic Analysis With Human Researchers in the Japanese Clinical Context and Its Cultural Interpretation Challenges. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2025;27:e71521.
papers.dataset: 30 Japanese patient/provider semi-structured interviews at urban and rural hospitals; average duration 28.43 and 24.33 minutes; topic sacred moments.
papers.run_design: Each interview three times; additional Charmaz grounded-theory and Pope five-step framework prompts.
papers.human_reference: Independent reflexive thematic analysis; saturation after 27; 20% second-researcher recoding; member checking.
papers.principal_results: Common descriptive themes over 80% agreement; culturally nuanced/low-frequency categories such as no-experience and fate below 30%; GPT fate count zero; less frequent themes inconsistent.
papers.statistics: No kappa because structured presence/absence unavailable.
papers.ethics_privacy: Shimane KS20230706-1; written consent; reuse authorization; anonymized/password-protected repository; vendor/API retention/transmission not reported.
papers.review_implication: Direct evidence of low-frequency and cultural-nuance loss.

papers.citation: Wachinger et al. Prompts, Pearls, Imperfections: Comparing ChatGPT and a Human Researcher in Qualitative Data Analysis. Qualitative Health Research. Online 2024;35(9), 2025 issue.
papers.dataset: One coauthor-to-coauthor 58-minute English interview, over 7,000 words, about AI in clinical practice; six chunks via third-party ChatGPT Splitter.
papers.run_design: General thematic-analysis prompt repeated three times; Charmaz and Framework prompts.
papers.principal_results: No systematically stronger same-prompt overlap; manufactured transcript continuation; two nonexistent verbatim quotes; silently altered quotes; convincing but potentially unfitting theoretical mapping.
papers.review_implication: Failure-mode evidence for chunking, prompt stability, fabricated provenance, and theory-induced circularity.

papers.citation: Ronaghi et al. Large Language Models for Large-Scale, Rigorous Qualitative Analysis in Applied Health Services Research. arXiv:2601.14478. 2026.
papers.dataset: 167 multi-site federally qualified health-center interviews about diabetes care.
papers.workflow: Human-LLM framework combining qualitative synthesis of researcher summaries and deductive coding to refine an intervention.
papers.models: not reported in this track's verified extraction
papers.metrics_statistics: not reported in this track's verified extraction
papers.ethics_privacy: not reported in this track's verified extraction
papers.full_text_uncertainty: Only primary preprint HTML/abstract-level verification was completed; do not use for detailed quantitative synthesis without renewed full-text extraction.

papers.citation: Elangovan A, He J, Verspoor K. Memorization vs. Generalization: Quantifying Data Leakage in NLP Performance Evaluation. EACL 2021:1325-1335.
papers.principal_result: Similarity-stratified evaluation; SST-2 accuracy 85.0 in least-overlap input bin versus 96.8 in most-overlap bin.
papers.review_implication: Use participant/source-disjoint splits and report performance by nearest training/reference similarity.

papers.citation: Liu et al. Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts. Transactions of the ACL. 2024;12:157-173.
papers.principal_result: U-shaped position effect; evidence in the middle of long contexts is used less reliably than evidence near beginning/end.
papers.review_implication: Randomize transcript/chunk/participant/rare-case positions and report survival sensitivity.

papers.citation: Lu et al. Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them: Overcoming Few-Shot Prompt Order Sensitivity. ACL 2022:8086-8098.
papers.principal_result: Exemplar order ranges from near-state-of-the-art to near-random; good order does not transfer; entropy selection produced 13% relative improvement across 11 classification tasks.
papers.review_implication: Permute codebook definitions, demonstrations, transcript chunks, and theme-list order.

papers.citation: Zhao et al. Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models. ICML 2021.
papers.principal_result: Few-shot predictions exhibit majority-label, recency, and common-token biases; contextual calibration mitigates them.
papers.review_implication: Temperature zero is not a substitute for order/format controls and calibration.

papers.citation: Deng et al. Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models. NAACL 2024.
papers.principal_result: ChatGPT and GPT-4 exactly guessed a missing MMLU option 52% and 57% of the time.
papers.review_implication: Probe public clinical theme references with missing-theme guessing, canaries, placebos, and blinded labels rather than merely noting possible contamination.

papers.citation: Balloccu et al. Leak, Cheat, Repeat: Data Contamination and Evaluation Malpractices in Closed-Source LLMs. EACL 2024.
papers.principal_result: Approximately 4.7 million samples from 263 benchmarks were estimated to have been exposed to OpenAI models in the first year through API use/applicable policies, plus evaluation and reproducibility malpractices.
papers.review_implication: Uploading gold themes/evaluation data can create privacy and future-contamination risk; archive vendor policy at study time.

papers.citation: Morris et al. Text Embeddings Reveal (Almost) As Much As Text. EMNLP 2023:12448-12460.
principal_results: 92% of 32-token inputs reconstructed exactly; BLEU 97.3.
89% of full names reconstructed from MIMIC clinical-note embeddings.
papers.review_implication: Treat hosted embeddings and vector stores as sensitive raw text.

papers.citation: Baroud et al. Beyond De-Identification: A Structured Approach for Assessing and Reducing Privacy Risks in Clinical Text. PrivateNLP 2025.
papers.dataset: 100 MIMIC-III discharge summaries; 6,199 indirect-identifier annotations across 9 categories.
papers.principal_result: Explicit-PHI deidentification does not eliminate indirect contextual identifiers.
papers.review_implication: Audit combinations of dates, occupations, family events, sites, diagnoses, and quotations for residual reidentification.

papers.citation: Van Aken et al. What Do You See in this Patient? Behavioral Testing of Clinical NLP Models. ClinicalNLP 2022.
papers.principal_result: Models with similar aggregate AUROC can behave drastically differently under demographic counterfactuals.
papers.review_implication: Apply demographic/source counterfactual swaps and residual-error tests to qualitative outputs.

evidence: Yu et al. show repeated identity can dominate representation similarity and predictions.
Ashwin et al. found no interviewer-identity effect in their corpus but found respondent-linked error.
Mathis merged interviewer and participant turns.
Hill explicitly excluded facilitator speech yet facilitator coding drove many errors.
Bai/Finkelstein supplied disease background and did not ablate it.
identity_source_domain.gap: No located core clinical paper jointly reports participant-, site-, interviewer-, and diagnosis-disjoint evaluation, source-probe accuracy, and counterfactual identity/source swaps.

evidence: Sakaguchi reports omission/instability of low-frequency culturally specific themes.
LLM-TA reports overrepresentation of rare dramatic experiences.
Ashwin reports respondent-linked systematic errors and downstream bias.
minority_negative_cases.interpretation: Failure is bidirectional: omission, dilution, misattribution, and sensational overrepresentation.
minority_negative_cases.gap: No located clinical paper operationalizes both participant-level evidence coverage and controlled negative-case survival.

stability.finding: Repeated-run agreement is analytically distinct from evidential validity and demographic fairness.

contamination.observed: General benchmark contamination is empirically established in adjacent NLP.
contamination.clinical_status: Reviewer-inferred risk, not demonstrated contamination: several clinical papers reuse publicly described themes/corpora and disease labels with pretrained systems; no direct clinical contamination probe was located.
minimum_controls: different-family verifier only as secondary evidence

strong_practices: Vikan: explicit LLM-specific participant information and offline sensitive server.
Prescott: refused third-party upload absent authorization.
Hill: written consent, separate secondary-use choice, secure institution, transcript withheld for residual identifiability.
risks: Deidentification does not remove indirect identifiers.
Embeddings can reveal raw clinical text and names.
Consumer/proprietary service retention, training use, BAA, processor/subprocessor, data region, and deletion are often not reported.
Local inference still needs access control, logging, and residual-identification review.
ethics_privacy.accountability: Humans must remain responsible for interpretation, evidence verification, stopping, publication, and downstream decisions; evaluator independence and participant/member validation should be designed, not assumed.

efficiency.finding: Inference latency alone understates total cost.

open_gaps.candidate: Participant/source/domain-confound and negative-case audit for clinical thematic analysis
open_gaps.minimum_differentiator: Fresh/private multi-site corpora; participant/site/interviewer/diagnosis-disjoint evaluation; source probes and counterfactual swaps; controlled rare/negative cases at varied positions; participant-level provenance/fairness metrics; independent blinded evaluation.
Unpublished codebook/reference; availability timeline; disease/name masking; canary, placebo, paraphrase, and missing-theme probes; preregistration.

open_gaps.candidate: Privacy-utility audit of local versus approved API qualitative coding
open_gaps.minimum_differentiator: Empirical indirect-identifier and embedding-inversion attacks; local 70B versus approved enterprise API; processor/retention/consent model cards; subgroup utility analysis.

open_gaps.novelty_risk: high if limited to repeated prompting
open_gaps.minimum_differentiator: Order and position crossed with source cues, rare-case frequency, and negative-case survival.
Prospective role randomization; independent qualitative/domain/participant adjudicators; override/stopping logs; downstream decision impact; total audit cost.

recommended_project.title: Whose Voice Survives? Auditing Participant, Source, and Negative-Case Confounds in LLM-Assisted Clinical Thematic Analysis
